rv.q: The aim here, for sure, was an updating of the standard wedding farce, and so achieved, given the various eleventh-hour arrivals of courage and a remarkably fluid set of sexual orientations that allow for a fresh mix-and-matching of couples.
An excellent cast transcends the sometimes predictable material.
Seriously, it’s OK to laugh — although you may hate yourself in the morning.
It's the sort of show that practically redefines the term “guilty pleasure.”
Right now, lyrics that say we've "seen it all before" are the truest words in the show.

There’s not an element in “It Shoulda Been You” that hasn’t been used, and wrung dry, before.

Hie thee to the Brooks Atkinson theatre to witness Ms. Daly surrounded by a slew of delightful performances in what is Broadway's best cast comedy.

'It Shoulda Been You' the delightfully giddy, goofy musical comedy, this Broadway season's freshest and funniest to date, defies skepticism, both in its wacky humor and its big, buoyant heart. The 100-minute 'Shoulda Been' can feel like a revival of some lost screwball classic.
“It Shoulda Been You” may strike some as ‘been there done that,’ but I bet you have never seen it done with this much talent!

A Jewish bride marries a Christian groom, overbearing mothers go to war, the older sister feels left out and there are countless hitches on the way to getting hitched. If you think you've heard this one, you're only partly right.

“It Shoulda Been You,” which opened Tuesday at the Theatre in New York, suffers the reverse problem — terrific book, numbingly bland music — which in the crazy world of musical theater does not KO its chances for success.
Overall, this is fair-to-middling material that’s elevated by a superior cast.
It Shoulda Been You is sometimes about as fresh as a week-old danish and the score (by Barbara Anselmi and Brian Hargrove) is largely uninspired.
Unfortunately, at its core It Shoulda Been You is ridiculously unbelievable, and the major shift in action sets the show on a course from which it can never recover.
Weaknesses still remain, led by the contrived story and a decidedly non-rousing score, but what was well-nigh intolerable in New Jersey is now... well, tolerable.
But this is Broadway. "It Shoulda Been You" shoulda been better.
Even without those interruptions, though, it would be hard to get on board with the clumsy tale.

Even if Hargrove’s gags were funnier, or Barbara Anselmi’s score more noteworthy, they could not make up for the absence of any authentic-feeling observations about love or commitment or weddings or…anything.
When the material is this disappointing, no one can save it.
By the time it was over, It Shoulda Been You had gained my respect, and I found I’d had a most enjoyable time.
'It Shoulda Been You' is a guilty treat of a musical that I couldn't help liking.

"This is a musical comedy with big theater names and remarkably forgettable music and lyrics — when walking out of the theater, I couldn’t name a single song I just heard. But I did have fun...The plot appears deceptively simple.
Nevertheless, the cast’s energy yukking it up through quick-moving sequences lifts the production and makes this largely formulaic storyline funny.
It Shoulda Been You, a trifling production that coulda been so much more.
Unsurprisingly this casting comes as a detriment that highlights the show’s unnerving need to please all and failure to please anyone.

cn.t: A wedding farce with talented pros (Tyne Daly, Harriet Harris) elevating creaky stereotypes and forgettable music. Critics find it mildly amusing but dated, though a surprising plot twist earns points for trying something fresh.
